8	/-!
9	# DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound
10	
11	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
12	and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **finite dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`,
13	there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**
14	Weil divisors `D`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes:
15	
16	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`:
17	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.
18	
19	This is the **P5-uniform** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md`
20	§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
21	`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
22	locus.
23	
24	## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)
25	
26	The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
27	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
28	`D₀ = 0`:
29	
30	* FLV-fiber at `D₀ = 0` (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) gives `n₁` with
31	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;
32	* `0 < deg F` (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`) makes `b := n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` a legal
33	  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
34	  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
35	* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
36	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
37	  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.
38	
39	Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,
40	and `b` depends only on `(Y, π)` — exactly the shape DAT-D consumes.
41	-/

61	/-- **DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound.** For a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`
62	compatible with the structure morphisms, there is a single threshold `b : ℤ`, depending only on
63	`(Y, π)`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes for **every** Weil divisor `D` of
64	degree `≥ b`:
65	
66	`∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.
67	
68	The bound is `b = n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)`, with `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and `n₁` the FLV-fiber
69	threshold at `D₀ = 0`; see the module docstring for the collapsed route
70	(`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §4 DAT-0a). Consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist. -/
71	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1
72	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
73	    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
74	    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
75	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :
76	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D →
77	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
78	  obtain ⟨n₁, hn₁⟩ :=
79	    subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ (0 : Y.CurveDivisor)
80	  have hd'pos : 0 < CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
81	    zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor π
82	  refine ⟨(n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) + 1
83	      - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K), fun D hD => ?_⟩
84	  -- the residual class `[D] · [F]^{-n₁}`
85	  set c : Y.CechPic := CurveDivisor.picClass K D
86	    * (CurveDivisor.picClass K (fiberWeilDivisor π) ^ n₁)⁻¹ with hc
87	  have hcdeg : classDeg K c
88	      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
89	    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
90	    ring
91	  -- an effective witness of the residual class
92	  obtain ⟨W, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
93	  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
94	    have hWeq : CurveDivisor.deg K W
95	        = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
96	      rw [← hcdeg, ← hWc, classDeg_picClass]
97	    linarith
98	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hWdeg
99	  -- the witness divisor `n₁ • F + E` is in the class of `D`
100	  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)
101	      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
102	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_nsmul, hEc, hWc, hc,
103	      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
104	  -- base vanishing at `n₁ • F`, peel `E`, transport along the class
105	  have hbase : Subsingleton
106	      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π)) 1) := by
107	    have h := hn₁ n₁ le_rfl
108	    rwa [zero_add] at h
109	  have hpeel : Subsingleton
110	      (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π + E)) 1) :=
111	    peel_effective (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π) E hEnonneg hbase
112	  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K hclass hpeel
113	
114	end Uniform
115	
116	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.Finiteness
10	
11	/-!
12	# FLV-2(b) + FLV-3 — the H¹-quotient identification and the fibrewise large-twist vanishing
13	
14	The heart of the Wave-4 fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing campaign
15	(`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §§2.1, 2.3, bricks FLV-2(b) and FLV-3), for the curve
16	bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a field `K`)
17	with a dominant affine morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and its fiber divisor
18	`F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVFiberToolkit`).
19	
20	## The identification (FLV-2(b))
21	
22	On the affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, the general-coefficients
23	two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — its two affine vanishing instances
24	discharged by the quasi-coherence packaging of `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVQcoh` —
25	computes `H¹` of the twisted sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` as a cokernel of section modules. This
26	file identifies that cokernel with a quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap lattice
27	`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` (constant in `n`, by the landed overlap-constancy
28	`divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap`) by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` of
29	`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVLattice`, comapped through `N.subtype` — the one
30	submodule-of-submodule bridge of the campaign, paid once behind the named submodule
31	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeOverlap` (worksheet discipline (2)):
32	
33	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeH1Equiv :
34	  HModule (𝒪(D + n·F)) 1 ≃ₗ[K] N ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n`.
35	
36	## The endgame (FLV-3)
37	
38	`Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top` is the pure linear-algebra
39	stabilization: an increasing `ℕ`-chain of submodules with join `⊤` whose base has
40	Noetherian quotient is eventually `⊤` (images in the quotient by the base stabilize by
41	`monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian`, and the stabilized value must be everything).
42	Instantiated with `Aₙ` inside `N`:
43	
44	* the chain is increasing (`fiberLattice_mono`) and exhausts `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`,
45	  THE EXHAUSTION of FLV-1 — pole clearing at the finite fiber over `[1 : 0]`);
46	* `N ⧸ A₀` is finite-dimensional: it is `H¹(𝒪(D + 0·F))` through the identification, and
47	  every divisor sheaf has finite `H¹` by the landed dévissage
48	  (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`, `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiFiniteness`)
49	  — the only place the base finiteness (properness) inputs enter;
50	
51	so `Aₙ = ⊤` for all large `n`, and through the identification the twisted `H¹` is a
52	subsingleton — **the fibrewise large-twist vanishing**
53	(`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1`): per-class
54	`n₀`, no duality, no `R¹f_*`. The worksheet-shaped form for a finite dominant `π`
55	compatible with the structure morphisms
56	(`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) discharges the base
57	`H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input from finiteness of `π`
58	(`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`).
59	-/

69	/-- **Noetherian stabilization of an exhausting chain.** An increasing `ℕ`-chain of
70	submodules whose join is everything and whose base term has Noetherian quotient is
71	eventually everything: the images of the chain in the quotient by the base term stabilize,
72	and the stabilized image must be the whole quotient. This is the pure linear-algebra
73	endgame of the fibrewise large-twist vanishing (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §2.1). -/
74	theorem Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top {R : Type u} {M : Type v}
75	    [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {A : ℕ → Submodule R M} (hmono : Monotone A)
76	    (hsup : ⨆ n, A n = ⊤) [IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)] :
77	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, A n = ⊤ := by
78	  set f : ℕ →o Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0) :=
79	    ⟨fun n => (A n).map (A 0).mkQ, fun a b hab => Submodule.map_mono (hmono hab)⟩ with hf
80	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ :=
81	    monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian.mpr ‹IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)› f
82	  have hftop : f n₀ = ⊤ := by
83	    have h1 : ⨆ n, f n = ⊤ := by
84	      have h2 : ⨆ n, f n = Submodule.map (A 0).mkQ (⨆ n, A n) :=
85	        (Submodule.map_iSup _ _).symm
86	      rw [h2, hsup, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_mkQ]
87	    have h3 : ∀ m, f m ≤ f n₀ := fun m => by
88	      rcases le_total m n₀ with h | h
89	      · exact f.mono h
90	      · exact (hn₀ m h).ge
91	    have h4 : (⊤ : Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0)) ≤ f n₀ := by
92	      rw [← h1]; exact iSup_le h3
93	    exact le_antisymm le_top h4
94	  refine ⟨n₀, fun n hn => ?_⟩
95	  have hfn : (A n).map (A 0).mkQ = ⊤ := by
96	    have h5 : f n = ⊤ := by rw [← hn₀ n hn]; exact hftop
97	    exact h5
98	  have hcomap := congrArg (Submodule.comap (A 0).mkQ) hfn
99	  rwa [Submodule.comap_map_mkQ, Submodule.comap_top,
100	    sup_eq_right.mpr (hmono (Nat.zero_le n))] at hcomap
101	
102	end Stabilization

126	    Submodule K (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)) :=

128	    (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype

132	    s ∈ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n ↔ (s : Y.functionField) ∈ fiberLattice π D n :=

138	    Monotone (fiberLatticeOverlap π D) := fun _ _ h =>
139	  Submodule.comap_mono ((monotone_nat_of_le_succ (fiberLattice_mono π D)) h)

142	`Aₙ` fills the whole of `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`. -/
143	theorem iSup_fiberLatticeOverlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) :
144	    ⨆ n, fiberLatticeOverlap π D n = ⊤ := by
145	  rw [eq_top_iff]

147	  have hs : (s : Y.functionField) ∈ ⨆ n, fiberLattice π D n := by

166	sections of `𝒪(D')` on the π-charts: restriction preserves values, so the difference map
167	computes the literal difference in `K(Y)`. -/
168	private lemma divisorVal_moduleDiff (D' : Y.CurveDivisor)
169	    (t : ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₀ π)))
170	      × ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₁ π)))) :
171	    divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
172	        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff (Y.divisorSheaf K D') t)
173	      = divisorVal K t.1 - divisorVal K t.2 := by
174	  have hov : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
175	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
176	  have h1 : divisorVal K
177	      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
178	        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
179	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₂.op).hom t.1) = divisorVal K t.1 :=
180	    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.1
181	  have h2 : divisorVal K
182	      (((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.map
183	        (Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
184	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).f₁₃.op).hom t.2) = divisorVal K t.2 :=
185	    divisorPresheaf_map_val K _ hov t.2
186	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.moduleDiff_apply, divisorVal_sub, h1, h2]

189	/-- **The range of the two-cover difference map is the fiber lattice** (the general-`F`
190	restatement of the landed structure-sheaf `range_diff_eq` of
191	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.Finiteness`, assigned to FLV-2 by the worksheet §2.3): a
192	section of `𝒪(D + n·F)` on the overlap is a difference of restrictions from `V₀` and `V₁`
193	exactly when its underlying rational function lies in
194	`Aₙ = 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀) ⊔ 𝒪(D + n·F)(V₁)`. -/
195	private lemma range_moduleDiff_eq_comap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
196	    LinearMap.range ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
197	        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
198	        (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)))
199	      = (fiberLattice π D n).comap
200	          (divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
201	            (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype := by

/-!
# The ported ledger speaks about *this* project's genus

The χ-ledger of `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Ledger/` was ported from the sibling project
`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, and its Euler characteristics are taken on the
sibling's cohomology carrier: `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule` at `Type u`, over the *small*
Zariski site.  This project's frozen genus (`AlgebraicJacobian/Genus.lean`) is taken on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.HModule` at `Type (u+1)`, over a general site.  Those are the
`Ext`-modules of two *different* universe annotations, so `ChiCurve.lean` deliberately states
its results about a local `ledgerGenus` rather than silently reusing the name `genus`.

This file closes that gap, and the closure is genuinely cheap:

* `moduleKSheaf_eq_toModuleKSheaf` — the two structure sheaves are **definitionally equal**
  (`rfl`).  So only the universe annotation differs, not the sheaf being resolved.
* `ledgerGenus_eq_genus` — the two genera are **equal as natural numbers**, by
  `Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` (`Cohomology/MayerVietorisCore.lean`), which is this
  project's `k`-linear refinement of mathlib's bare `Abelian.Ext.chgUniv`.  `finrank` of
  linearly equivalent modules agree.
* `chi_divisorSheaf_genus`, `riemann_inequality_genus` — the ledger's two headline curve
  statements, restated with `genus C`.

## What this does and does not settle

It settles the *numerical* comparison, which is all the ledger needs: the ledger's content is
Euler characteristics and section-space dimensions, and those are `finrank`s.  It does **not**
produce a `LinearEquiv` between `Scheme.HModule` and `Sheaf.HModule` as stated — the carriers
live in different universes, so no such equivalence is even statable — and it does not claim
the two cohomology theories agree in any structured (functorial, long-exact-sequence) sense.
Anything needing naturality across the two carriers still has real work to do.

The predecessor audit (`RiemannRoch/LedgerPortability.lean`, inbox `I-0495`) predicted exactly
this: the universe gap is an *annotation*, because the ledger is a ledger of dimensions.  This
file is that prediction discharged rather than asserted.

## Provenance

AJC-native.  Nothing here is ported; it is a comparison between the ported material and this
project's own frozen definition, proved with this project's own `chgUnivLinearEquiv`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]

/-- **The two projects' structure sheaves are definitionally equal.**  The ledger resolves
cohomology against `Scheme.moduleKSheaf k` (small site, `Type u`) and this project's `genus`
against `Scheme.toModuleKSheaf` (general site, `Type (u+1)`); the *sheaf* is the same object,
and only the `Ext` universe annotation differs. -/
theorem moduleKSheaf_eq_toModuleKSheaf (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    C.left.moduleKSheaf k = Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C := by
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  rfl

/-- **The ledger's genus is this project's genus** (★): `ledgerGenus C = genus C`.

Both are `Module.finrank k` of an `Abelian.Ext` in degree one, against the same constant sheaf
and the same structure sheaf (`moduleKSheaf_eq_toModuleKSheaf`); they differ only in the
universe at which `Ext` is annotated, and `Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` is a `k`-linear
equivalence between those two annotations.  `finrank` does not distinguish linearly equivalent
modules, so the two natural numbers coincide.

This is what licenses reading the ported ledger's `1 - ledgerGenus C + deg D` as a statement
about the genus of `C` as this project defines it. -/
theorem ledgerGenus_eq_genus (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    ledgerGenus C = genus C := by
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  show Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
      = Module.finrank k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1)
  exact (Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv (R := k)).finrank_eq

/-- **Riemann–Roch-lite for the challenge curve, on this project's genus** (★):
`χ(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C + deg D`.

This is `chi_divisorSheaf_curve` with `ledgerGenus` replaced by `genus` along
`ledgerGenus_eq_genus`.  The binders are the three curve hypotheses only: the two
`Module.Finite` cohomology binders of the conditional ledger are *synthesised* here
(`moduleFinite_hModule_zero`, `moduleFinite_hModule_one`), not assumed. -/
theorem chi_divisorSheaf_genus (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (D : C.left.CurveDivisor) :
    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
    Sheaf.chi (C.left.divisorSheaf k D) = 1 - genus C + Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k D := by
  have h := chi_divisorSheaf_curve C D
  rw [ledgerGenus_eq_genus C] at h
  exact h

/-- **The Riemann inequality on this project's genus**: `deg D + 1 − genus C ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))`.
Same discharge as `chi_divisorSheaf_genus`. -/
theorem riemann_inequality_genus (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (D : C.left.CurveDivisor) :
    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k D + 1 - genus C
      ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (C.left.divisorSheaf k D) : ℤ) := by

  rw [ledgerGenus_eq_genus C] at h
  exact h

statement above for the trivial reason that `Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space
is `0`. -/

    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) := by
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
    moduleFinite_hModule_one C

    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=

  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=

      isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2)

theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness (W₀ D : Y.CurveDivisor)
    (hW₀ : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W₀) 1))
    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W₀ + 1 - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K)
      ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
  set c : Y.CechPic :=
    CurveDivisor.picClass K D * (CurveDivisor.picClass K W₀)⁻¹ with hc
  obtain ⟨Wc, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
  have hWcdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K Wc
      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - CurveDivisor.deg K W₀ := by
    rw [← classDeg_picClass K Wc, hWc, hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv,
      classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]
    ring
  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Wc + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    rw [hWcdeg]; linarith
  obtain ⟨E, hE0, hEc⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass Wc hWdeg
  have hclass : CurveDivisor.picClass K (W₀ + E) = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, hEc, hWc, hc,
      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]
  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K hclass
    (peel_effective W₀ E hE0 hW₀)

end Peeling

9	/-!
10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
11	
12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right

17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
20	
21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
22	over a field, proper over that field.
23	
24	## Main definitions
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
31	
32	## Main theorems
33	
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
41	
42	## Notes
43	
44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
47	-/

49	set_option autoImplicit false

51	universe u
52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
58	  -- smooth curve
59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
60	  -- proper
61	  [IsProper C.hom]
62	  -- geometrically irreducible
63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
73	
74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
75	
76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
82	  assoc := Category.assoc

84	-- data
85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=

93

95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=

117	  sorry
118

120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
121	  sorry

124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
126	  sorry

129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
134	  sorry

136	/--
137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
140	-/
141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
147	  sorry
148	
149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
156	  map _ := sorry
157	  map_id := sorry
158	  map_comp := sorry

160	end Jacobian

162	/-! ## Base change of fields
163	
164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
167	
168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
169	-/
170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
173	
174	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
176	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
177	
178	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
179	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
180	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
181	
182	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
183	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
184	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
185	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
186	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
187	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
188	
189	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
190	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
191	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
192	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
193	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
194	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
195	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
196	
197	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
198	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
199	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
200	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
201	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
202	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
203	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
204	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
205	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
206	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
207	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
208	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
209	
210	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
211	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
212	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
213	  eqToIso (by
214	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
215	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
216	
217	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
218	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
219	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
220	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
221	  eqToIso (by
222	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
223	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
224	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
225	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
226	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
227	
228	namespace Jacobian
229	
230	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
231	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
232	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
233	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
234	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
235	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
236	    (e : C ≅ C') :
237	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
238	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
239	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
240	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
241	
242	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
243	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
244	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
245	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
246	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
247	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
248	  sorry
249	
250	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
251	
252	/-- Identity coherence. -/
253	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
254	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
255	    baseChangeIso k k C =
256	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
257	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
258	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
259	  sorry
260	
261	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
262	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
263	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
266	    baseChangeIso k M C
267	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
270	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
271	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
272	  sorry
273	
274	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
275	
276	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]

278	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

281	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
282	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
